newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Lend Lease has union deal on CFM bid.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Lend Lease has union deal on CFM bid.

text.p: Property and financial services group Lend Lease Corp said it had reached an agreement for the key public sector union to have a stake of up to five percent in Commonwealth Funds Management (CFM) if its bid is successful.

The Australian government said in May this year it would sell CFM, which has about A$8 billion under management, with a decision expected towards the end of 1996. Market analysts have said the winning bidder would probably pay about A$100 million.
Apart from Lend Lease, other companies interested in CFM include ING Bank unit Mercantile Mutual and Australia and New Zealand Banking Group Ltd.
Lend Lease investment director Bill Webster said the company had struck two agreements with the Community and Public Sector Union (CPSU), which has about 120,000 members.

One deal involved the provision of financial advice to CPSU members. "Secondly, should it be successful in its bid for Commonwealth Funds Management, Lend Lease has agreed to provide for formal union representation on the board of the new funds management company and grant the CPSU the opportunity to take up to a five percent stake in the company in the future," he said.
